## Report and scope

Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1200

Reproduce the reported dry-run/apply disagreement after a legitimate post-receipt comment. Preview must run the same exact-snapshot proof and expose the same refusal code without mutating history. The earlier remediation-registry fix does not own this per-stream proof discrepancy.

## Reported reproduction

## Summary

`pm merge reconcile --dry-run` and `pm merge reconcile` disagree about the same unchanged inputs, in the direction that makes the dry run useless: the preview reports success for streams the real run then refuses. The divergence is deterministic and reproduces on every invocation.

Reproduced on **@unbrained/pm-cli 2026.9.5** (also present on 2026.9.2).

## Observed

Same working tree, no edits between the two commands:

```
$ pm merge reconcile --dry-run --json
ok: False | totals: {'repaired': 2, 'skipped_clean': 0, 'failed': 0}
   pm-linear-unfa -> repaired
   pm-linear-4yle -> repaired

$ pm merge reconcile --json
ok: False | totals: {'repaired': 0, 'skipped_clean': 0, 'failed': 2}
   pm-linear-unfa -> failed  Merge receipt evidence for pm-linear-unfa does not prove the exact item snapshot (no_receipt_set_proves_snapshot).
   pm-linear-4yle -> failed  Merge receipt evidence for pm-linear-4yle does not prove the exact item snapshot (no_receipt_set_proves_snapshot).
```

`repaired: 2 / failed: 0` becomes `repaired: 0 / failed: 2`. Every per-stream `outcome` flips from `repaired` to `failed`.

## Why this matters

The dry run's stated contract is to preview the real run, and its own guidance tells the operator to rely on it:

> `Review repair.streams, then rerun pm merge reconcile without --dry-run to apply audited repairs.`

An agent following that guidance concludes two streams will be repaired and proceeds. Nothing is repaired. Because the failure is about **evidence sufficiency** rather than about writing, the dry run could determine it just as well as the real run — the check is simply not being applied on the preview path.

Note the dry run is not merely optimistic in aggregate: it individually labels each stream `repaired`, which is the field an agent would parse to decide.

## Expected

`--dry-run` should apply the same receipt-evidence validation as the apply path, so a stream that will fail with `no_receipt_set_proves_snapshot` is previewed as `failed` with that same error. If the evidence check genuinely cannot run without writing, the preview should report the outcome as undetermined rather than as `repaired`.

## Detail worth keeping

Both flagged receipts are of the shape `requested_preference: ours`, `conflict_resolution: stable_value_order`, and both sit in `.git/pm-merge-receipts/` while the item files received later legitimate `comment_add` events. That later edit is what makes the receipt no longer prove the current snapshot — a completely ordinary sequence for a multi-agent repository, so this is the common case rather than a corner case.

`git status` stays clean across both invocations, so the apply path writes nothing when it fails; the divergence is purely in reporting.

## Environment

- @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.9.5, Node 22, Linux
- 80 items / 83 history streams, 2 clone-local receipts

## Delivery boundary

Intake only in PR #1204. This item remains open and unclaimed; no implementation or reproduction success is asserted. Implement through the public SDK with thin CLI adapters and executable negative controls before closing.
